item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
…attempting to enter Keter containment chambers.

This has an interesting implication. In order to do this, Dorian must somehow know that what's in the room is deadly. Maybe it has an inverted "spider sense" to sniff out danger. Or maybe it shares knowledge from the current owner. But I think it would be more interesting if Dorian just overheard staff shop talk. That would mean it not only understands English but is smart enough to work out what "Keter" means from context. Or at least to figure out that the most heavily secured rooms are most likely to serve its self-destructive purpose. A fully intelligent kitty makes its depression all the more impactful, IMO.

Also, I propose that A███ S███████'s last name be extended by 3 black boxes. So it could plausibly be covering up "Schrodinger". :P

item.content:encoded: Everything MrUnimport said back in June of 2009 is perfect. There's no stated reason for the skip to be consistently suicidal other than possible depression (which cats can get, to be fair) and it fits the theme of Dorian Grey much better to have the skip be a typical danger-prone cat and have all damage transfer to its paired owner. Lots of story potential there, too. I mean, even without understanding the character of Dorian Grey and how fitting an allusion that would be, it would make for better writing.

One of my biggest pet peeves is describing the discovery and recovery of an SCP object before actually obtaining the SCP object. This article does it in just such a weird and obnoxious way that I have to downvote from that alone.

That aside, I also don't like that this is intentionally suicidal and tries to kill its owners intentionally.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I don't know why, but I really don't like the "suicidal" aspect. I've had cats that were stupid, careless, clumsy, and even belligerent to the point of doing suicidal things; but never one that just actively tries to kill itself. I think it would be much more believable if the cat was just oblivious. It gets killed on a regular basis simply because it runs through life getting into EVERYTHING. Personally it would also make it much more unsettling for me. Being accidentally killed because something else just doesn't think before doing anything…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Suggestion for improvement: make the cat invincible, instead of regenerating, with injuries inflicted to its body-double being the injuries it would have received, not just equivalent. Perhaps, to further the Dorian Gray allusion, the cat's owner should exhibit signs of aging at a slightly accelerated rate, while the cat feels nothing. Furthermore, erase signs of the cat being homicidal: instead, it has simply learned it is utterly invincible, with no real grasp of the human cost of its thrill-seeking ways.

Actually, making the cat simply enjoy throwing itself into danger is a better Dorian Gray reference than making it murderous.

item.title: Re:

Really? Because I thought I was being helpful. Let me elaborate.

The very best SCP articles, I think, are the ones that are not directly malevolent, but are dangerous by nature. You suffer not because it's trying to kill you but simply because of what it is.

This one tries too hard to be scary but it's just dumb.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Having one's life tied to a somewhat capricious life form is a unsettling idea. That being said, I've never really been overjoyed with this entry. The tone is a little off, and the cruel nature of the cat seems…unnecessary. I grew up in the country, and have had cats all my life. Between possums, eagles, raccoons, tall trees, drainage pipes, speeding cars, and a myriad of other things, a cat has no need for a cruel intelligence to almost die on a daily basis.

Now, if you made it more of a normal cat, and added damage sharing, then you may be on to something. A example would be if the cat got a leg split open during a fight with something, and the owner suddenly gets a gaping wound as well. The cat gets hit, and suddenly the owner gets splattered all over the area he was in.

item.title: My first SCP...
item.content:encoded: I'd been thinking of how different Dorian Grey's life would've been if he'd used some sort of pet instead of a painting. My first thought was dog, but that's a bit dull… then I thought, what about an intellegent, self aware cat? Being at the mercy of a cat would be terifying.
